name: Tan Ruiqing
current_role: Major shareholder (approx. 6.8%) of Lomon Billions Group (SZSE: 002601); former vice chairman (left board April 2023)
profile: Tan Ruiqing is a co-founding shareholder and former vice chairman of Lomon Billions Group, one of the world's largest titanium dioxide pigment makers, which grew out of a state-owned sulfur mine business in Jiaozuo, Henan. He left the board at the April 2023 re-election but still held ~162m shares (6.81%) per an April 2026 filing.
interesting_fact: Lomon Billions grew out of a state-owned sulfur/brimstone mine business in Henan and became a leading global supplier of titanium dioxide pigment (the white in paint, plastics and paper).
notes: No longer a director or executive; very low public profile. IR email is from the 2022 annual report summary (securities representative Wang Haibo, still listed in 2026 report); best route is via Lomon Billions board office in Jiaozuo. Shares partly pledged per 2026 filing.

name: Sara Liu
current_role: Co-founder, Senior Vice President and Director, Super Micro Computer Inc. (Supermicro)
profile: Sara Liu co-founded server and storage maker Supermicro with her husband, CEO Charles Liang, in San Jose in 1993; it went public in 2007 and is now a major supplier of AI/GPU server systems built around Nvidia chips for data centers. She remains a senior vice president and board director.
interesting_fact: Liu was Supermicro's treasurer from its founding in 1993 until 2019 and its chief administrative officer over the same period, effectively running the company's finances through its growth from startup to public AI-server giant.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a B.S. in accounting from Providence University in Taiwan, and also served as Supermicro's SVP of Operations from 2014 to early 2018.
notes: Very relevant to a data-center podcast but rarely gives interviews; husband Charles Liang is the public face. Route via Supermicro PR.

name: Liu Suling
current_role: Director and Vice President, Guangdong Naruida Radar Technology Co. (SSE STAR: 688522); co-actual controller
profile: Liu Suling (Su Ling Liu), a Canadian citizen, co-founded phased-array weather radar maker Naruida in Zhuhai in 2014 with her husband Bao Xiaojun; they jointly control it via holding company Jiazhongtong. Naruida makes X-band dual-polarization active phased-array radars for weather and rainfall monitoring and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023. She has been a director and VP since Dec 2020.
interesting_fact: Naruida reached 100m+ yuan revenue within about five years of founding and became the niche leader in phased-array weather radar; its radars are used for meteorology and flood/rainfall monitoring, with expansion into civil aviation, ocean monitoring and forest-fire detection.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding a radar company, Liu (who holds a master's degree) spent nine years doing statistics work in Canada, per Naruida's IPO prospectus; her co-founder husband was a Raytheon Canada engineer.
notes: Input lists industry as 'Defence' but Naruida is primarily civil weather/hydrology radar. Low public profile; route via board secretary Gong Xuehua / IR@naruida.com.

name: Ji Zhe
current_role: CEO and Executive Director, Wasion Holdings (HKEX: 3393); director of Willfar Information Technology (SSE STAR: 688100)
profile: Ji Zhe is the son of Wasion founder Ji Wei and co-holder with him of the family stake in Wasion Holdings, a Changsha-based smart-meter and energy-measurement group, and its ~58%-owned STAR-listed IoT/grid-communications unit Willfar. He joined Wasion's board in 2014 and became CEO and executive director in June 2022; he chaired Willfar from 2017 to 2022.
interesting_fact: Wasion and Willfar supply smart electricity meters, energy-IoT and power-grid communication systems, making Ji a second-generation operator in China's grid-digitalisation and energy-data business.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business, Ji earned an economics degree from the University of British Columbia (2007) and spent 2007-2011 as a manager in Macquarie Group's equity capital markets division.
notes: Sources conflict on whether he currently chairs Willfar (36Kr says chairman; insider-data sites say director only since late 2022). Good fit for energy/grid topics. IR email is Willfar's (board secretary Zhong Xiyu).

name: Zhang Yan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai i2Finance Technology Co. (I2SOFT, BSE: 920799)
profile: Zhang Yan (b. 1975) co-founded Shanghai i2Finance in 2009 with Wu Zhen; together they control ~50% of the Beijing Stock Exchange-listed firm. i2Finance builds core banking, e-banking, AI and VR/'xinchuang' (domestic-tech) software for Chinese banks and says it serves all 21 systemically important banks. He has been chairman and GM since 2020.
interesting_fact: i2Finance says its software now reaches all 21 of China's systemically important banks and 31 trillion-yuan-asset commercial banks, including all six big state-owned lenders.
deep_cut_fact: A Beijing Institute of Technology computer-science graduate, Zhang started as a product manager at Yunnan Nantian Electronics (1998-2000) and then ran the online-banking division as a VP at Yusys Technologies (2001-2008) before founding i2Finance.
notes: Input's 'Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)' tag could not be matched to i2Finance (which is listed); possibly a different venture. IR email is board secretary/CFO Wang Tao's, as published in the 2025 annual report.

name: Yang Meihua
current_role: Director, Shenzhen Jame Technology Corp. (JMT, SZSE ChiNext: 300868); co-founder and co-controlling shareholder
profile: Yang Meihua (b. 1982) co-founded Shenzhen-based Jame Technology, which designs and manufactures protective cases for smartphones, tablets and wearables for major device makers and its own brands; it listed on ChiNext in 2020. She and her husband, chairman Chen (Shen) Jianping, are the controlling shareholders; she previously served as deputy GM and is now a board director.
interesting_fact: Jame grew from a 2006 start into a listed maker of phone, tablet and wearable cases and watch straps, supplying global device makers, leading accessory brands and international retail chains.
deep_cut_fact: Per Jame's annual report, Yang was born in 1982 and co-founded the company with a vocational secondary-school (zhongzhuan) education, serving as deputy general manager before moving to the board.
notes: Partner's surname is written 谌 (Shen/Chen) Jianping in filings. Very low public profile; route via board secretary Zhou Bo (zb@jamepda.com per 2024 annual report) or ir@jamepda.com.

name: Mu Jinxiang
current_role: Actual controller (controlling shareholder) of Lianhe Chemical Technology (SZSE: 002250); former chairwoman
profile: Mou (Mu) Jinxiang, b. 1954, co-founded Lianhe Chemical Technology in Taizhou, Zhejiang, in 1985 with her husband Wang Zhihua; it makes crop-protection, pharmaceutical and specialty-chemical intermediates and listed in Shenzhen in 2008. She became a billionaire in 2015 on the stock's rise; she has since stepped back from the chair but remains the company's actual controller.
interesting_fact: Forbes named her one of Asia's 50 Power Businesswomen in 2016, and Forbes in 2013 highlighted her as a self-made Chinese woman entrepreneur on the move.
deep_cut_fact: She built Lianhe from a 1985 start in Taizhou into a supplier of custom-synthesised agrochemical and pharma intermediates for global life-science companies, taking it public on the Shenzhen exchange in 2008.
notes: Name also written Mou Jinxiang (牟金祥 on Wikipedia vs 牟金香 in input). Retired from chair; very private. Route via Lianhe board secretary office. No IR email verified (web-search quota exhausted). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Wu Cheng Hsueh
current_role: Founder of Gourmet Master Co. Ltd. (TWSE: 2723), operator of 85°C Bakery Cafe (current board title not verified)
profile: Taiwanese entrepreneur Wu Cheng-hsueh incorporated Gourmet Master in 2003 and opened the first 85°C Bakery Cafe in New Taipei in 2004. The coffee-cake-bakery chain expanded to Australia (2006), mainland China (2007) and the US (2008, Irvine CA), reaching roughly 1,000 stores worldwide; the Cayman-registered parent is listed in Taiwan.
interesting_fact: The chain's name comes from Wu's belief that 85°C (185°F) is the optimal temperature at which to serve coffee.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2017 the company's US central kitchen in Brea, California became its first solar-powered facility worldwide, a neat energy hook for the podcast.
notes: 85mkt@ is the marketing/partnership inbox (not strictly press). IR contact window exists on InvestorRelations pages of 85cafe.com. Input lists country as China but he is Taiwanese. Current board role not re-verified (web-search quota exhausted).

name: Yoshiyuki Aikawa
current_role: Chairman and CEO, SBC Medical Group Holdings Inc. (Nasdaq: SBC)
profile: Dr. Yoshiyuki Aikawa, 55, is a Japanese cosmetic surgeon who opened Shonan Beauty Clinic in Fujisawa in 2000 and grew it into SBC Medical Group, a management-services business for a large network of aesthetic clinics in Japan. SBC listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger with Pono Capital Two in September 2024; he is chairman and CEO and its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: A single private clinic opened in Fujisawa in March 2000 became a Nasdaq-listed group after a 2024 de-SPAC; Aikawa remains chairman/CEO and sold shares as selling stockholder in an April 2026 offering.
deep_cut_fact: Aikawa graduated from Nihon University Medical School in 1997, trained in anaesthesiology (member of Harvard Medical School's PostGraduate Assembly of Anesthesiology) and served as president of the Japanese Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery in 2014-15.
notes: SEC filing states stockholder communications to the board go via ir@ir.sbc-holdings.com. Not a natural fit for energy/data-center themes; entrepreneurship angle (clinic to Nasdaq).

name: Chen Jiangtao
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Beijing Watertek Information Technology Co. (SZSE ChiNext: 300324); not on current board
profile: Chen Jiangtao founded Beijing Watertek Information Technology in 1997; the ChiNext-listed company does embedded-system testing, electronic-component screening, tax/finance information-security platforms and smart-city work. He remains its actual controller (~5.1% direct stake at end-2025), while Chen Weiqun has chaired the company since November 2020.
interesting_fact: Watertek's 2025 annual report says it is repositioning around AI computing-power infrastructure, AI industry applications and the 'low-altitude economy' (drones/eVTOL), which overlaps with the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Watertek, Chen held about 8.98 million shares (1.16%) of payments company Lakala (300773) at end-2025, per Watertek's annual report.
notes: Shared-wealth partner in input is Liu Xiping (also a Watertek shareholder). Company reported a loss in 2025. Route via board secretary Cai Houfu / investor@watertek.com.

name: Shao Heng
current_role: Shareholder of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group (SZSE: 002602); current executive role not verified
profile: Shao Heng (a Hurun Under-40 listee 2019-2022) derives his wealth from Century Huatong, the former auto-parts maker that became a major Chinese online-games group. He and Wang Ji are named as commitment parties from Century Huatong's 2014 asset restructuring, in which it acquired game developers Qiku Network and Tianyou Software; it later bought DianDian/Century Games and Shengqu Games.
interesting_fact: Century Huatong evolved from auto parts into games (2014-2019) and then added an internet data-center business with projects in Shenzhen and Shanghai (2020-21), a direct link to the podcast's data-center theme.

name: Zhang Huawei
current_role: Former chairman of Shandong Weigao Group Medical Polymer (HKEX: 1066), resigned March 2021; long-time general manager/chairman of parent Weigao Holding (current title not verified)
profile: Zhang Huawei (Zhang Hua Wei) is a veteran of Weihai-based Weigao (Wego), China's large medical-consumables group (infusion sets, syringes, orthopaedics, blood-purification products). He was deputy factory director of Weigao Holding from 1988, its general manager from 1998 and chairman of the HK-listed medical-polymer arm until stepping down in March 2021.
interesting_fact: Weigao grew from a small Weihai factory into one of China's biggest medical-device makers; Zhang was there from 1988, running the parent's operations as general manager from 1998.
deep_cut_fact: While already a deputy factory director at Weigao, Zhang studied politics and economics at Shandong University's Weihai campus (1996-1998), per Weigao's 2019 annual report.
notes: Resignation as 1066 chairman effective 30 March 2021 (2021 annual report: https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2022/0510/2022051000547.pdf). csc@weigaogroup.com is Weigao's general service-centre inbox, not a personal office. Founder of Weigao is Chen Xueli; Zhang is a senior executive/shareholder.

name: Tse Kam Pang
current_role: Founder and former co-chairman of Royale Home Holdings (HKEX: 1198), stepped down as executive director Aug 2025; appointed chairman of Regal Partners Holdings (HKEX: 1575) in Oct 2022
profile: Hong Kong businessman Tse Kam Pang founded the Royale furniture group in 1997, building it into a mattress and home-furnishings maker and retailer selling in China; it is now partly owned by Guangzhou's state-linked Science City Group. He chaired Royale (co-chairman from 2023) until resigning as a director on 4 Aug 2025.
interesting_fact: Before founding Royale in 1997 he was deputy managing director of a Hong Kong listed company, and he has 30+ years in international and China trade.
deep_cut_fact: He has served as a vice chairman of the Hong Kong Furniture Association, per Royale's 2024 annual report.
notes: No longer on Royale's board (resigned Aug 2025; avoid probing reasons). info@royale.com.hk is Royale's published company email. Current status at Regal Partners not re-verified. Aged ~71.
